content.text: The verifier's substantive review confirms the analysis: the compliant classification, the absence of any audit right, and the no-redline posture are all endorsed. The only failure is the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check, which the verifier itself notes is expected because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency limit. I'll resubmit with tightened paragraph citations and rationale that make the "no clause exists" basis explicit rather than appearing to rely on paragraphs that contain no audit right.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale:
No audit, inspection or verification right exercisable by Kubient against the Customer exists anywhere in this Agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "records" and "books" each returned zero results across the single section (sec-preamble), and a full read of all 75 paragraphs confirms it. The nearest language is unrelated to verification: p0001 (quoted) is ordinary cooperation for service delivery, p0002 is the licence granted to Customer, p0025 restricts Customer from giving third parties access to the Service, and p0035/p0045 are database security representations. Nor is there any Customer self-reporting or record-keeping obligation an audit right would police: Impressions are "measured by Kubient" itself (p0009) and, under section 5, revenue flows from Kubient to Customer on a sequential-liability basis.

Because AUDIT constrains a Vendor right that burdens our party, the complete absence of that right leaves us with no audit exposure at all, which is at least as favourable as the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access). None of the walk-away triggers are present: there is no unlimited or unannounced audit right and no Vendor remote access to Customer systems. No redline is proposed, since inserting frequency, notice and cost limits would first have to create a Vendor audit right that does not exist today and would worsen our position.

Sub-elements noted for the file, not flagged: the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check cannot be satisfied because there is no clause to bear a frequency cap. Forward-looking watch item only: section 1 contemplates Services defined in individual Exhibits and section 5 lets Exhibits override the default fee mechanics, so if any Exhibit later introduces Customer-side reporting or a fee true-up, we should then negotiate the preferred limits, with the 15-day notice / 10% underpayment fallback available.
